items.followUp: What is decision making in problem solving?

rubric.why: Decision making involves choosing among possible options.
rubric.description: Defines decision making as making a choice.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that decision making involves choosing or selecting an option.

rubric.why: A suitable decision is made from available alternatives with the problem requirements in mind.
rubric.description: Mentions the alternatives or requirements considered.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning available alternatives or the problem requirements.

modelAnswer: Decision making is the process of choosing the most suitable option from available alternatives.
The choice is made by considering the requirements of the problem.

items.followUp: Explain the function of the AND operator.

rubric.why: NOT is a logical operator that operates on one Boolean value.
rubric.description: Identifies NOT as a logical unary operator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying NOT as a logical operator or unary operator.

rubric.why: NOT reverses the truth value of its operand.
rubric.description: Explains how NOT changes a Boolean value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that NOT changes TRUE to FALSE and FALSE to TRUE, or otherwise reverses a Boolean value.

modelAnswer: NOT is a logical unary operator that acts on one Boolean value.
It reverses the value: TRUE becomes FALSE, and FALSE becomes TRUE.

items.followUp: What is volatile memory? Give one example.

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory preserves its stored data when power is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that non-volatile memory retains or keeps its data.

rubric.why: The defining feature is that stored data remains even when the device has no power.
rubric.description: States the condition under which data is retained.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the data remains when power is off or unavailable.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its stored data even when the power is switched off.
Examples include ROM and flash memory.
